rationale: All three review lenses (blind, edge-case with repo access, acceptance against plan.md ACs) ran and returned parseable output; all six acceptance criteria pass and the IDOR is closed at the router layer mirroring the established update/delete handlers. Three 'major'-labeled items were reviewed and DEFERRED as defense-in-depth, not live defects: (1) TOCTOU double-load — SettingsTester re-loads by the same setting_id; the only window is delete+reinsert-of-same-UUID, not realistic, and the actual IDOR path is rejected 403 before SettingsTester runs (SettingsTester explicitly out of scope per plan). (2) Falsy setting_id bypass — verified non-exploitable: SettingsTester.__init__ (line 61) uses the IDENTICAL `if request.setting_id:` predicate as the router guard (line 274), so an empty-string id loads credential_values=[] (inline behavior) and never loads a stored credential; there is no input that both skips the guard and loads a victim's setting. (3) `except ExtendedHTTPException: raise` forwarding non-4xx codes — matches the existing codebase pattern; speculative. Also deferred: null setting_type defaulting to USER (fail-closed hardening, acceptance lens low). One test-hygiene nit (config.ENV mutated local->dev without restore) matches the pre-existing pattern in sibling tests and did not affect the passing 47-test run. Dismissed: 0. Deferred: 5 (suitable for a follow-up hardening ticket). No patch or decision_needed findings remain. Confidence medium (not high) because multiple majors were flagged-and-deferred rather than absent; recommend a follow-up ticket to harden SettingsTester (pass the authorized setting object, add None guard, validate setting_id non-empty).
